paper_title: On Knowledge Compilation for Two-Variable First-Order Logic
statement: Another natural question is whether our method can be extended to FO3 ? Such an extension is nontrivial. The feature of two variables is used in an essential way throughout our method. First, models of FO2 can be organized by unary types and binary types, which makes the two-stage decomposition possible. For FO3 , constraints relate more elements simultaneously, so pairwise type compatibility is no longer sufficient. Second, our extendability checks rely crucially on the bounded configuration characterization of Theorem 14. This is closely related to the classical boundary between the well-behaved two-variable fragment and richer fragments with three or more variables. Therefore, instead of targeting unrestricted FO3 directly, a promising direction is to study extensions of FO2 such as counting extensions like C2 or FO2 with additional restricted axioms, e.g., tree or linear order axioms.
context: It is well-known that the order of variable branching can significantly affect the performance of propositional compilers, such as c2d and cudd. In our proposed method, we use a restricted processing order. It first branches unary types and then binary types. We remark that this restriction is not merely an implementation choice but is crucial for the efficiency of the method, more specifically for the efficiency of extendability checks. Interleaving unary and binary type decisions would break the symmetry and make the extendability checks even fall back to the #P-hardness of FO2 satisfiability with arbitrary binary evidence [28]. We however note that recent work on FO2 model counting with binary evidence that is of bounded treewidth [18] may provide a promising direction for extending the method to handle more flexible processing orders, that we leave for future work. Another natural question is whether our method can be extended to FO3 ? Such an extension is nontrivial. The feature of two variables is used in an essential way throughout our method. First, models of FO2 can be organized by unary types and binary types, which makes the two-stage decomposition possible. For FO3 , constraints relate more elements simultaneously, so pairwise type compatibility is no longer sufficient. Second, our extendability checks rely crucially on the bounded configuration characterization of Theorem 14. This is closely related to the classical boundary between the well-behaved two-variable fragment and richer fragments with three or more variables. Therefore, instead of targeting unrestricted FO3 directly, a promising direction is to study extensions of FO2 such as counting extensions like C2 or FO2 with additional restricted axioms, e.g., tree or linear order axioms. The last potential direction is to combine the type-level approach of our method with finer-grained propositional compilation techniques, which is suggested by our experiments on ΓP and u4-b2-fo. The current compiler operates primarily at the level of types, and may therefore miss finer-grained propositional independence in some instances.
